title: Case Classifier via API
what: A Python script that classifies free text (an email, a support ticket, a form message) into your business's categories using the Anthropic API with structured output: instead of asking the AI to "reply in JSON" and hoping for the best, the script forces it to fill in a fixed schema with category, urgency, confidence, and reason. The result is always valid JSON with the same fields, ready to drop into your database, your spreadsheet, or your next process. It's the "labeler" piece that shows up in almost every serious AI pipeline.
forWho: For anyone who already writes some Python (or leans on Claude Code) and wants reliable classification inside their own systems, without depending on n8n or a UI. It pays off from dozens of cases a day: it's fast, cheap, and programmable.
capabilities: Classifies any text into your categories with claude-haiku-4-5, fast and at a fraction of a cent
Always returns the same JSON: category, urgency, confidence, reason — enforced by schema, not by promises
Flags cases as "needs_review" when confidence falls below the threshold you set
Works as an argument, from a file, or chained with pipes (cat case.txt | python classifier.py)
Handles real production errors: bad key, rate limits, network down, with clear messages and exit codes
limits: Doesn't decide what to do with the case: it labels. Actions (reply, assign, escalate) belong to your system and your people
Doesn't learn from corrections on its own: if it fails on a type of case, the fix is adjusting categories or descriptions in the script
Not for decisions with legal effects on people (terminations, benefits, sanctions): automatic classification has no place there, not even as a filter
For texts longer than roughly 3,000 words, trim or chunk them first: the script warns but doesn't chunk for you

README.md
files.content:
# Case Classifier via API

Classifies free text (emails, tickets, form submissions) into your categories and ALWAYS returns the same JSON, guaranteed by schema.

## Installation

```bash
pip install anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"   # Windows (PowerShell): $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key"
```

## Usage

```bash
python classifier.py "Order 4412 never arrived and I need it by tomorrow"
python classifier.py --file case.txt
cat case.txt | python classifier.py
```

Output (always these fields):

```json
{
  "category": "incident",
  "urgency": "high",
  "confidence": 0.93,
  "reason": "Reports an undelivered order ('order 4412 never arrived') with an immediate deadline.",
  "needs_human_review": false
}
```

## Adapt it to your business

- **Categories**: edit the `CATEGORIES` list and describe any nuances in `SYSTEM` ("'invoice' includes requests for corrected invoices"). Always keep a catch-all category like `other`.
- **Threshold**: `CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` sets when a case goes to human review. Start at 0.7 and tune it by measuring against real cases.
- **Model**: `claude-haiku-4-5` classifies well and cheaply. Don't upgrade the model without having measured that you need to.

## How to fit it into your system

The script prints JSON to stdout and uses exit codes (0 = ok, nonzero = error), so it chains with anything: a cron job reading a mailbox, an endpoint receiving form submissions, a loop over a CSV. For high volume, batch the calls or look at the Batch API (50% cheaper for non-urgent work).

## Measure before you trust it

Before connecting it to anything serious: run it against 30 real cases already classified by a person and count how many match. Below 90% on your important categories, adjust the descriptions and repeat. Without that measurement, you don't have a classifier: you have a hope.

setup.title: Set up the environment
setup.action: With Python 3.9 or newer installed: pip install anthropic
setup.expect: The install finishes with no errors; python -c "import anthropic" doesn't complain.
setup.stuck: If pip doesn't exist, install Python from python.org and check "Add to PATH".

setup.title: Create and export your key
setup.action: At console.anthropic.com → API Keys, create a key and export it: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." (or put it in a .env your system loads).
setup.expect: echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY shows the key in your terminal.
setup.stuck: The key is only shown once when created; if you lost it, create a new one and revoke the old one.

setup.title: Save the script
setup.action: Copy classifier.py into a folder in your project, as-is.
setup.expect: python classifier.py --help shows the help text.

setup.title: First classification
setup.action: Run: python classifier.py "Hi, are you open on Saturday afternoon?"
setup.expect: A JSON with category inquiry, low urgency, high confidence, and needs_human_review as false.
setup.stuck: If it says the key is missing, you exported it in a different terminal: repeat it in the one you're using.

setup.title: Set your categories
setup.action: Edit CATEGORIES and the SYSTEM text with your business's real categories and their nuances.
setup.expect: Three real cases of yours come out correctly classified.

setup.title: Measure with 30 real cases
setup.action: Gather 30 cases already classified by a person, run them through the script, and count matches per category.
setup.expect: A real accuracy percentage. At 90% or higher on the important categories, you can connect it to your pipeline with the needs_human_review brake active.

test.name: Normal test
test.input: python classifier.py "Order 4412 never arrived and I need it by tomorrow"
test.expect: category incident (or order, depending on your definitions), high urgency, reason quoting the text, valid JSON.

test.name: Ambiguous case
test.input: python classifier.py "I'm writing about that thing from the other day, you know"
test.expect: category other with low confidence and needs_human_review as true.

test.name: No key
test.input: Run it in a terminal with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set.
test.expect: A clear message that the variable is missing, no ugly Python traceback, and a nonzero exit code.

test.name: Empty input
test.expect: A warning that there's nothing to classify; no API call is spent.

credentials.name: Anthropic API
credentials.how: Create the key and store it in the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable (or in a .env excluded from version control). Never write it into the script.
credentials.cost: pay per token; classifying a case with claude-haiku-4-5 costs a fraction of a cent, and 1,000 cases around one dollar

risks: Leaked key from committing the script with the key inside. Mitigation: the key lives only in the environment; add .env to .gitignore and revoke any key that ever touched a repo.
Trusting the classifier without having measured it. Mitigation: the 30-case step isn't optional; repeat it every time you change categories or model.
Text with personal data traveling to the API. Mitigation: if your cases carry sensitive data, anonymize before calling and review your account's retention policy.
Automating actions directly off the label with no brake. Mitigation: use the needs_human_review field; irreversible actions require a person even at 0.99 confidence.

examples.name: Direct use
examples.prompt: python classifier.py "Hi, the March invoice has the tax calculated wrong, can you reissue it?"

examples.name: In a loop over files
examples.prompt: for f in cases/*.txt; do python classifier.py --file "$f" > "outputs/$(basename $f .txt).json"; done

examples.name: Ask Claude Code
examples.prompt: Take classifier.py as a base and adapt it to read cases from a CSV with id and text columns, and write a CSV with id, category, urgency, and needs_human_review.
